model: INDRA SimpleScorer form (INDRA belief engine: https://indra.readthedocs.io/en/latest/modules/belief/index.html), applied separately to supporting and to contradicting evidence

formula.per_class: P_wrong(s) = min(1, syst_s + rand_s ^ n_s), n_s = number of INDEPENDENT items of source class s; a class with no items contributes factor 1
formula.support: E = 1 - PROD_s P_wrong(s) over supporting items
formula.contradiction: R = 1 - PROD_s P_wrong(s) over contradicting items

independence: Items are deduplicated by their source key before counting: one DOI or PMID counts once however many drafts cite it; one pre-registered test counts once across its readings and its evidence drafts (key = the claim id of the test); one language model counts once (key = assessor name); one Lean conflict counts once (key = the law id).

preregistered-test.what: claim-tests/**/result.json verdict supports (support) or refutes (contradiction); mixed adds one item to each side; inconclusive adds nothing and is reported

repo-evidence.what: an unsigned nanopub draft in a thread folder, not derived from a claim test, whose declared status is supported / established / observed (support) or refuted / not-established (contradiction), keyed by draft file

literature.what: a DOI or PMID cited by a SUPPORTING draft for this record (the draft cites it as a source; this pipeline did not re-read the paper for direction of support)

model-elicitation.what: a language-model truth score from truth/raw via docs/claims.json: p_true >= 0.5 is one supporting item, p_true < 0.5 one contradicting item. An elicited opinion, never a measurement; high syst because the models share training data

lean-conflict.what: a law linked to the claim is 'contested' or carries open_conflicts in lean/registry (contradiction only)

not_used: A Lean proof of the claim's mathematical reading: it proves a model's consequence, not that organisms obey the model. Already-formalized claims leave the queue instead.
Testability / dataset-resolvability: how easy a claim is to test is not evidence that it is true; used only as a queue tie-break.
Prior work found by nanopubs-index searches but not cited by any draft: not read for direction of support.
calibration: The rand/syst values are set by hand and have NOT been fitted. INDRA fits them to curated statement corpora; this project has no curated LeanBio corpus yet. Treat belief as an ordering heuristic for the formalization queue, not a probability.

queue.order: formalizable 'theorem' before 'named-hypothesis', then belief desc, then supporting preregistered tests desc, then testability desc, then id
